text:
Taylor H: Hey team — first week trouble ticket: migrated from Docker Desktop to Colima and my local postgres container refuses to start: error in logs "could not create lock file \"/var/lib/postgresql/data/postmaster.pid\": Permission denied". I'm using a host bind mount to ~/dev/pgdata. Also weirdly Redis intermittently returns ERR NOAUTH even though REDIS_PASSWORD is set in .env. Any quick pointers?

Ravi: hi Taylor, welcome! two separate but common issues. For Postgres + Colima, host bind mounts can show up owned by root inside the VM. We usually use a named docker volume for dev to avoid host-uid woes.

Ravi: Quick fixes:
```bash
# 1) chown the host dir inside colima to postgres uid
colima ssh
sudo chown -R 999:999 /home/someuser/dev/pgdata
exit
# 2) restart the service
docker-compose up -d db
```

Lina: if you must keep the host mount (eg for seed SQL), alternative is to run the container as uid 999 so files created match expected owner: `user: "999:999"` on the db service. Not ideal but handy for short-term dev.

Taylor H: I tried chown in colima and postgres started, thanks! But my init scripts that CREATE EXTENSION pgvector fail with: "could not open extension control file \"pgvector.control\"". I didn't change the image — using `postgres:15-alpine` in compose. Could alpine be missing packages?

Ravi: yep alpine images often don't have apt/pkg manager for the usual .deb packages. Our repo's dev image is Debian-based and installs the pgvector package. Use the same dev Dockerfile or switch to a non-alpine image. Example Dockerfile snippet we use: 
```Dockerfile
FROM postgres:15
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y postgresql-15-pgvector
```

Lina: alternatively, use the upstream pgvector extension from source (pgxn/compile) but that's more work. For quick parity with our CI/dev environment, match the image tag in the runbook.

Taylor H: Redis issue: I checked and `docker-compose exec redis env | grep REDIS` shows the variable present, but my app still gets ERR NOAUTH. Running `docker-compose exec redis redis-cli -a "$REDIS_PASSWORD" ping` gives PONG. Could be multiple redis instances running locally?

Ravi: Yep check `docker ps` for stray redis containers. Also ensure your app's compose file points to the same redis service and that the client library is configured to send AUTH. If you're using separate compose override files, note which .env is loaded. `docker compose --env-file .env.dev up` vs `docker-compose` behaviour can differ depending on CLI.

Lina: quick commands: 
```bash
docker ps --filter ancestor=redis --format "table {{.Names}}\t{{.Image}}\t{{.Status}}"
docker-compose exec redis redis-cli -a "$REDIS_PASSWORD" ping
docker-compose exec redis env | grep REDIS
```

ops-bot: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/local-db-setup — section "Colima & host mounts" and "PG extensions in dev images". Also note our recommended compose snippet uses a named volume for db and the repo dev image.

Taylor H: Great — switched to the repo dev image and a named volume and the pgvector init runs fine now. Also found I had an old redis container from a previous compose file; removed it and the app auth issue disappeared. Thanks everyone!

Ravi: nice. If you want, paste the minimal steps you ran and we'll add them to the runbook for Colima users.

Taylor H: Will do and happy to pair if anyone has 10 mins. Appreciate the help :smile:
